title: Mean, median and mode
meaning: Mean, median and mode are three ways to describe a "typical" value. The mean is the plain average, the median is the middle value once the data is sorted, and the mode is the value that appears most often.

Analysts pick the one that fits the data: the mean for evenly spread numbers, the median when a few extreme values (or ordered ratings) would distort the mean, and the mode for categories such as colours or regions.

formula.spoken: x bar, the mean, equals the sum of the values divided by n, the number of values

symbols.meaning: sigma x: add up every value
"x bar", the usual symbol for the mean

steps: Sort before finding the median. With an odd count, it is the middle value.
With an even count, average the two middle values: the median of 1, 3, 5, 7 is (3 + 5) ÷ 2 = 4.
The one long 13-minute call pulls the mean up to 5, while the median stays at 3. The median is the better "typical" call here.

trap.wrong: Using the mean to describe skewed data such as salaries or house prices.
trap.why: A few very large values drag the mean away from where most of the data sits. The exam expects the median for skewed or ordinal data and the mode for categories.

title: Range, variance and standard deviation
meaning: These measure spread: how far the values sit from each other. The range is simply largest minus smallest. Variance and standard deviation measure the typical distance from the mean.
Analysts care because two data sets can share a mean and still behave very differently; a small standard deviation means values cluster tightly, a large one means they vary a lot.

formula.spoken: s, the sample standard deviation, equals the square root of: the sum of each value minus the mean, squared, divided by n minus 1

symbols.meaning: each value's deviation: how far it is from the mean
the deviation squared, so negatives do not cancel positives
add up all the squared deviations
for a sample, divide by one less than the count; for a whole population divide by n
the variance: the value before the square root, measured in squared units (minutes², dollars²)
the square root, which brings the units back to the data's units; this is the standard deviation

example.intro: A sample of five deliveries took 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 minutes. Find the range, sample variance and sample standard deviation.

x − x̄

steps: The deviations always add to 0, which is why we square them.
If these five were the whole population, divide by n instead: 40 ÷ 5 = 8, and √8 ≈ 2.83.

trap.wrong: Dividing by n when the data is a sample, or stopping at the variance when the question asks for the standard deviation.
trap.why: A sample uses n − 1; the exam signals it with words like "a sample of customers". The population formula (÷ n) is only for every member of the group. And the standard deviation is the square root of the variance, so check which one the question asks for.

title: Outliers, IQR and z-scores
meaning: An outlier is a value far from the rest. The interquartile range (IQR) rule and the z-score are two standard ways to decide what counts as "far".
Analysts check for outliers because they can be data-entry errors to fix, or real but rare events worth a closer look, and because they pull the mean away from typical values.

formula.text: IQR = Q3 − Q1;  fences = Q1 − 1.5 × IQR and Q3 + 1.5 × IQR;  z = (x − x̄) ÷ s
formula.spoken: IQR equals Q3 minus Q1. The lower fence is Q1 minus 1.5 times IQR, and the upper fence is Q3 plus 1.5 times IQR. The z-score equals the value minus the mean, divided by the standard deviation

symbols.meaning: the first quartile: a quarter of the sorted data is below it
the third quartile: three quarters of the data is below it
the spread of the middle half of the data
values below the lower fence or above the upper fence are outliers
how many standard deviations a value is from the mean; a value 3 or more standard deviations away (z of 3 or more, or −3 or less) is often called an outlier

example.intro: Order sizes have Q1 = 12 and Q3 = 20. One order has 40 items. Is it an outlier?

steps: 40 is above the upper fence of 32, so it is an outlier.
z-score idea: if the mean is 16 and the standard deviation is 8, then z = (40 − 16) ÷ 8 = 3, three standard deviations above the mean.
An outlier pulls the mean toward itself but barely moves the median.

trap.wrong: Adding 1.5 × IQR to the median, or using the range instead of the IQR.
trap.why: The fences are built from the quartiles: subtract from Q1 and add to Q3. The range includes the outliers themselves, so it cannot be used to find them.

title: Distribution shape and the 68-95-99.7 rule
meaning: A distribution's shape is what a histogram of the data looks like (a bar chart of how often each range of values occurs). A normal distribution is a symmetric bell; a skewed one has a long tail on one side.
Shape tells an analyst which summary to trust (mean for symmetric data, median for skewed) and, for normal data, how much of it falls near the mean.
rule: Normal (bell-shaped, symmetric): the mean, median and mode are about equal. About 68% of values lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean, about 95% within 2, and about 99.7% within 3. This is the 68-95-99.7 rule.
Right-skewed (long tail to the right, such as incomes): a few high values pull the mean above the median.
Left-skewed (long tail to the left, such as scores on an easy test): a few low values pull the mean below the median.
The skew is named after the side the tail is on, not the side the peak is on.

example.intro: Battery life is normally distributed with a mean of 10 hours and a standard deviation of 1 hour. What share of batteries last between 8 and 12 hours?

table.caption: The 68-95-99.7 rule for a mean of 10 and a standard deviation of 1
head: Range
Standard deviations from the mean
Share of values

steps: 8 is 10 − 2 × 1 and 12 is 10 + 2 × 1, so the range is the mean ± 2 standard deviations.
The rule gives about 95% of batteries in that range.
The remaining 5% splits evenly between the two tails: about 2.5% below 8 hours and 2.5% above 12.

trap.wrong: Calling data with a long tail to the right "left-skewed" because the peak is on the left.
trap.why: Skew is named for the tail. A long right tail is right-skewed (positive skew), and there the mean is greater than the median.
